title: Plating Bacteria to Isolate a Single Colony
author: Katy M Monteith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.u8cezsw

steps.title: Inoculate Bacteria in LB Broth
steps.instruction: Inoculate a small fragment of bacteria from either a frozen glycerol suspension aliquot or an agar media plate lawn into 10 mL LB broth in a 50 mL falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Use a sterile inoculation loop to collect the bacteria.
Shake the loop in the media until the fragment is loose and visibly floating.

steps.title: Incubate Overnight Culture
steps.instruction: Incubate the culture in an orbital shaker at 140 rpm for approximately 12-14 hours at 30/37 °C (depending on the species' optimal growth temperature).

substeps.instruction: Loosely replace the falcon tube lid and secure it with tape to allow aerobic conditions.

steps.title: Verify Bacterial Growth
steps.instruction: Check the media for cloudiness the following day to confirm growth.

substeps.instruction: If unsure, use an Absorbance Microplate Reader to check optical density; an O.D. of 0.6-0.8 is ideal (exponential growth phase).

steps.title: Prepare Agar Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare an LB agar plate (or a genus-specific media plate, e.g., Pseudomonas isolation media, to reduce contamination risk) and bring it to room temperature before use.

steps.title: Perform First Streak
steps.instruction: Using a sterile inoculation loop, dip into the overnight media culture and streak three discrete lines across the bottom of the agar plate.

steps.title: Perform Second Streak
steps.instruction: Using a new sterile inoculation loop dipped in sterile LB broth, streak three discrete lines at an adjacent angle from the initial lines.

substeps.instruction: The first line should cross all three initial bacteria lines.
The second line should cross two bacteria lines.
The third line should cross one bacteria line.

steps.title: Perform Third Streak
steps.instruction: Turn the plate 90° so the LB broth lines are at the bottom. Using a new sterile inoculation loop (without dipping into media), streak three discrete 'clean' lines at an adjacent angle from the LB broth lines.

substeps.instruction: The first line should cross all three LB broth lines.
The second line should cross two LB broth lines.
The third line should cross one LB broth line.

steps.title: Perform Fourth Streak
steps.instruction: Turn the plate 90° so the 'clean' lines are at the bottom. Using a new sterile inoculation loop (without dipping into media), streak three discrete 'clean' lines at an adjacent angle from the previous 'clean' lines.

substeps.instruction: The third line can be streaked into the center of the plate to spread the growth area.
Ensure these lines do not contact the original bacteria lines to prevent lawn growth.

steps.title: Incubate Plates
steps.instruction: Place the plates inverted in an incubator at 30/37 °C for approximately 24 hours.

steps.title: Evaluate Colony Growth
steps.instruction: Check for isolated colonies (typically ~1-2 mm diameter).

substeps.instruction: If growth is insufficient: leave for another 12-24 hours, or repeat the process dipping the loop in LB broth for the 3rd and 4th streaks.
If a lawn occurs: dilute the overnight liquid culture (e.g., add 40 mL sterile LB broth for a 1:4 dilution) before streaking.

steps.title: Isolate Single Colony
steps.instruction: Select an isolated colony and use a sterile inoculation loop to collect it and inoculate into 10 mL LB broth, ensuring no other colonies are touched.

substeps.instruction: Adjust LB broth volume based on downstream needs: 10 mL is sufficient for 100-200 μL glycerol aliquots; for re-inoculation, the overnight culture should be 10% of the final volume (e.g., 100 mL for a 1 litre final volume).

steps.title: Final Incubation and Verification
steps.instruction: Incubate the isolated colony culture in an orbital shaker at 30/37 °C and 140 rpm for approximately 12-14 hours under aerobic conditions.

substeps.instruction: After 12-14 hours, verify that the optical density is optimal (between 0.6-0.8) before proceeding to frozen stocks or experimental procedures.
